d626eef797180ef05dc08836d7e5a6ff4f52fe1b: Forni di Sopra is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 13 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Forni di Sopra has managed to preserve the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoilt landscapes and a human atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. Forni di Sopra's altitude (882 m at the base, 2,066 m at the top) helps it keep a decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The day lift pass at 44€ places Forni di Sopra among the intermediate resorts on budget: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short, Forni di Sopra does not rival the ski giants, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

d69abe8efd019c6ed6ff75a595b4a4f1c6b38bf1: The Grau Roig ski area, with its 215 km of runs, offers a fine choice for every type of skier: large enough not to go round in circles for a week, yet compact enough to find your favourite sectors easily. The 74 lifts let you link descents without long waits. Grau Roig's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Pyrenees for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2640 m and a village at 2100 m, Grau Roig's snow reliability is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but the situation improves quickly with the first serious snowfalls. The budget for a stay in Grau Roig is clearly high: 69€ for a day lift pass, on top of which come accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before setting off. In short, Grau Roig delivers on its promises. A Pyrenean resort that will suit most skiers without disappointing.
